summary:
Targeted retest of iteration 28's mono-tag color fix on ClientReview.jsx ReviewedState. Visited /r/FVMnmrqr2cWsANCh (share_status='rejected') and verified via getComputedStyle that both the

'CONCERNS DELIVERED' text and the AlertTriangle icon now resolve to rgb(239, 68, 68) — the CSS var --danger (#EF4444). Previous grey rgb(112,112,123) is gone. Inline style { color: var(--danger) } correctly overrides the .mono-tag { color: var(--text-3) } class rule due to inline-style specificity. Fix VERIFIED.
critical_code_review_comments: Fix correctly applied at ClientReview.jsx lines 763, 765, 769 — inline style ensures CSS var color wins over .mono-tag utility class regardless of cascade order.

Accepted-state path (DOCUMENT ACCEPTED + Check icon in --accent #5E6AD2) was not seeded/tested via UI but code path is symmetric and uses identical inline-style pattern, so behavior will be equivalent.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter 29 was a single-issue retest. Mono-tag color fix verified: p.color = rgb(239,68,68), svg.color = rgb(239,68,68), --danger resolves to #EF4444, --accent to #5E6AD2. Screenshot at .screenshots/reviewed_state.png shows red 'CONCERNS DELIVERED' tag with red AlertTriangle. Accepted path (DOCUMENT ACCEPTED in --accent blue) was not explicitly rendered but the code uses the same inline-style mechanism.
rca of the issue: Iteration 28 introduced .mono-tag CSS class with `color: var(--text-3)` which overrode Tailwind text-danger/text-signal utilities due to CSS source-order cascade. E1's fix in iter 29 replaced Tailwind color utilities with inline style={{ color: 'var(--danger)|var(--accent)' }}. Inline styles have higher specificity than any class-based rule, guaranteeing the intended color wins. Verified via computed style API.
